nodes.name: Every 3 minutes
nodes.notes: Was every 1 minute, which was shorter than the chain it starts. Even with the early claim, a poll faster than the work it kicks off is asking for a double-pickup.

nodes.name: Enrol email (no gate — see notes)
nodes.notes: Calls VIO-enrol-email, which has NO Slack approval. The approval still exists on VIO-agent-tool-push-instantly (VIOwfBpushinst1) for the agent path. See the comment in Shape for enrolment for why the two differ.

parameters.query:
-- Write the outcome back onto the lead, and record it in the ledger.
--
-- `channel_state_email` uses the SENDER's vocabulary, and 'dropped' is deliberately not in it:
-- that word belongs to verification and means "Reoon says this address is not real".
-- VIO-enrol-email refuses a dropped address outright as a verified negative no human may override,
-- so writing it here for "enrolment did not land" once locked a perfectly good lead out of the
-- pipeline permanently — gavriel.legynd@visioneerit.com on 2026-08-30, whose address was fine.
-- Two writers, one column, two vocabularies.
with p as (select $1::jsonb as j)
update leads l set
  channel_state_email = (p.j->>'channel_state_email')::vio_email_state,
  opener              = coalesce(p.j->>'opener', ''),
  email_draft         = coalesce(p.j->>'email_draft', ''),
  sendr_page_url      = coalesce(p.j->>'sendr_page_url', ''),
  updated_at          = now()
from p
where l.id = (p.j->>'lead_id')::uuid
returning l.id, l.contact_email, l.channel_state_email

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ lead_id: $json.row_number, channel_state_email: $json.channel_state_email, opener: $json.opener || '', email_draft: $json.email_draft || '', sendr_page_url: $json.sendr_page_url || '' }) }}

parameters.query:
-- One row per poller, overwritten each cycle. Not an events row: events is
-- append-only and is what the console reads, and a heartbeat every three minutes would bury the
-- ledger it exists to make readable.
with p as (select $1::jsonb as j)
insert into system_status (workflow, last_run_at, every_minutes, last_result, checked, waiting, ok, detail)
select p.j->>'workflow', now(), (p.j->>'every_minutes')::int,
       coalesce(p.j->>'last_result',''), coalesce(p.j->>'checked',''),
       nullif(p.j->>'waiting','')::int, (p.j->>'ok')::boolean,
       coalesce(p.j->'detail', '{}'::jsonb)
from p
on conflict (workflow) do update set
  last_run_at   = now(),
  every_minutes = excluded.every_minutes,
  last_result   = excluded.last_result,
  checked       = excluded.checked,
  waiting       = excluded.waiting,
  ok            = excluded.ok,
  detail        = excluded.detail
returning workflow, last_run_at, waiting

options.queryReplacement: ={{ JSON.stringify({ workflow: $json.workflow, every_minutes: $json.every_minutes, last_result: $json.last_result, checked: $json.checked, waiting: $json.waiting, ok: $json.ok, detail: $json.detail }) }}

parameters.query:
-- Claim exactly one lead, atomically, and report how many were ready.
--
-- THE CLAIM IS THE POINT. On the sheet a row was read, processed, and only then marked — and for a
-- good lead the mark did not happen until after its Sendr page was generated. Two overlapping polls
-- could take the same person and mail them twice. Here the UPDATE re-reads the row under its own
-- lock, so a second run sees `pending_approval` and matches nothing. It cannot be claimed twice.
--
-- `leads_ready` carries the state filter, the campaign check AND the suppression re-check, so a
-- person who landed on the never-contact list after being verified cannot be picked up by a future
-- edit here that forgets to look.
--
-- The count is taken in the same statement, before the update lands, so it says how many were
-- ready when this cycle started rather than a number from a separate round trip that may already
-- be stale.
with ready as (
  select count(*)::int as n from leads_ready
),
picked as (
  update leads l
     set channel_state_email = 'pending_approval',
         updated_at = now()
   where l.id = (select id from leads_ready order by created_at limit 1)
     and l.channel_state_email in ('not_sent', 'approved')
  returning l.*
)
-- LEFT JOIN so this returns exactly one row even when nothing was claimed: the heartbeat has to
-- run on an idle cycle too, and a query that returns nothing would stop that branch dead.
select r.n as ready_count, to_jsonb(p) as lead
  from ready r
  left join picked p on true

meta.idNote: id VIOwfDsheetdemo1 is historical. Renaming the workflow is safe; changing the ID is not — importing under a new id creates a SECOND workflow and leaves this one active, giving two schedules on the same Leads tab and duplicate sends.
